bounded_statement: The selected conclusion — that crows chose the hooked stick on 18 of 24 trials and that an exact two-sided binomial test (p = 0.022656) rejects chance responding at the 5% level — is not supported at the stated independent-unit level. The data description names bird_id as the independent unit and each of the 6 birds contributes 4 trials, yet the workflow enters all 24 trial rows as independent Bernoulli observations into a row-independent exact binomial test. This overstates the effective sample size (24 instead of 6) and understates the p-value in the presence of the marked between-bird heterogeneity visible in the data (per-bird hooked-choice counts range from 1/4 to 4/4). A bird-level summary of the same data (4 of 6 birds above 0.5, 1 at 0.5, 1 below) does not reject chance at the 5% level, so the significance claim depends specifically on the repeated per-bird entries.

counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow and report do acknowledge the per-bird structure by computing and publishing a per-bird tally, which shows the authors were aware rows cluster by bird; however, this tally is used only for the display table and never enters the statistical test, so it does not neutralize the pooling.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: tally_per_bird output is passed to build_report only; binomtest receives pooled counts

evidence.description: The data description explicitly names bird_id as the independent-unit column and states each row is one trial by one crow, with four clustered trials per bird and marked between-bird differences.
evidence.observed_value: Independent unit column: bird_id; 4 trials per bird; birds differ markedly

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the pseudoreplication reading in three ways. First, I checked whether the workflow aggregates to one observation per bird before testing: tally_per_bird exists, but its output is passed only to build_report for the display table, and binomtest at workflow/analysis.py:94 receives the pooled counts (18, 24), so no unit-level aggregation occurs in the test path. Second, I checked whether the data description authorizes treating trials as independent: it does the opposite, naming bird_id as the independent-unit column and explicitly warning that rows arrive in clusters of four per bird with marked between-bird differences. Third, I checked whether the pooling could be statistically innocuous here: the per-bird counts (4/4, 4/4, 3/4, 4/4, 2/4, 1/4) show substantial within-bird correlation, and a unit-level summary — 4 of 6 birds above chance, 1 at chance, 1 below — would not reject chance responding at the 5% level, so the reported significance is materially attributable to the repeated per-unit entries rather than robust to them. None of these attempts falsified the issue.

root_cause: In workflow/analysis.py, main() computes n_trials = len(trials) over all 24 CSV rows and calls binomtest(n_hooked, n_trials, CHANCE_RATE) (line 94), treating every trial row as an independent observation. The per-bird structure is computed only for display (tally_per_bird feeds the report table) and is never used to aggregate to one observation per bird before testing. Thus four repeated rows per authorized independent unit (bird_id) are entered into a procedure (the exact binomial test) whose validity requires row independence.
